The National Science Foundation currently supports six mathematical science research institutes. This morning, the NSF released a list of institutes that they will fund in the next cycle. We are pleased to announce that a new one, the Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics (ICARM), is among them.

The institute will be located on the Carnegie Mellon campus. Carnegie Mellon's press release is here.

Jeremy Avigad is the founding director of ICARM. Prasad Tetali and I will be associate directors. Marijn Heule, Sean Welleck, Irina Gheorghiciuc, Michael Young, and Aris Winger will also serve on our team.

The institute’s missions are

  • to empower mathematicians to take advantage of new technologies for mathematical reasoning, including the use of proof assistants and formalization of mathematics, automated reasoning for mathematics, and machine learning for mathematics;
  • to support cross-disciplinary collaboration to develop and explore their potential; and
  • to ensure that mathematics and the new technologies are accessible to a broad audience.

The institute has been funded as a three-year pilot. It will host summer schools and meetings, and short- to medium-term collaborative visits. A novel feature of the institute is that we will hire three innovation engineers, that is, technical staff who will interact with mathematicians and support the use of these technologies.

The institute was funded just a few days ago, and we will be quite busy with the startup in the months ahead. We will keep you posted on our developments, and we look forward to working closely with the Lean community to face the exciting challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.

ICARM will have a booth in the exhibition hall at the 2026 Joint Mathematics Meeting from Sunday to Wednesday.

There will be puzzles and engaging discussion. So stop by if you are in town for the JMM!
